message.content:
Below is a concise list of the **long‑weekend statutory holidays that occur in Canada during 2023**.  
A “long weekend” is defined as a holiday that falls on a Friday or a Monday, giving you a three‑day break (Friday‑Sunday or Saturday‑Monday).  

| Date (2023) | Holiday | Day of Week | Notes |
|-------------|---------|-------------|-------|
| **7 Apr** | Good Friday | Friday | Creates a 3‑day weekend (Fri‑Sun). |
| **20 Feb** | Family Day (Alberta, Saskatchewan, Ontario, Manitoba, New Brunswick, Prince Edward Island) | Monday | Long weekend for those provinces (Sat‑Mon). |
| **25 May** | Victoria Day | Monday | Long weekend (Sat‑Mon). |
| **7 Aug** | Civic Holiday (most provinces) | Monday | Long weekend (Sat‑Mon). |
| **4 Sep** | Labour Day | Monday | Long weekend (Sat‑Mon). |
| **9 Oct** | Thanksgiving | Monday | Long weekend (Sat‑Mon). |
| **25 Dec** | Christmas | Monday | Long weekend (Sat‑Mon). |

### Quick Summary

| Long‑Weekend Holiday | 2023 Dates (Fri‑Mon) |
|----------------------|----------------------|
| Good Friday | 7 Apr |
| Family Day (prov‑specific) | 20 Feb |
| Victoria Day | 25 May |
| Civic Holiday | 7 Aug |
| Labour Day | 4 Sep |
| Thanksgiving | 9 Oct |
| Christmas | 25 Dec |

> **Pro‑Tip:**  
> - If you’re planning trips in provinces that observe **Family Day**, you’ll have an extra long weekend in February.  
> - Some provinces also have other holidays that fall on a Friday or Monday (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Newfoundland & Labrador on 17 Mar, St. George’s Day in British Columbia on 23 Apr), but those are not nationwide and may not create a long weekend for everyone.

Feel free to plug this table into your holiday‑planning app, and let me know if you’d like province‑specific details or additional holiday information!
